bo.Transportation: Shared — FSS intervention lead + KSSN/resource coordination as needed
bo.Housing / basic needs: Shared — FSS intervention lead + KSSN/resource coordination
bo.Physical health: Shared — FSS intervention lead + School health role; KSSN if resource access is needed
bo.Mental health / school refusal: Shared — FSS intervention lead + School Behavioral Health/Counseling; KSSN if partner coordination is needed
bo.Academic access / challenge: School — school-controlled academic response, with FSS monitoring attendance/family voice
bo.Belonging / relationships: School — school-controlled belonging/relationship response, with FSS family/scholar voice
bo.Engagement / motivation: Shared — School engagement response + FSS scholar/family intervention; KSSN for opportunities when useful
bo.Safety / bullying / discipline: School — school-controlled safety/discipline response, with FSS attendance follow-through

Transportation: Warm connection to a community transportation resource when appropriate
Housing / basic needs: Warm handoff to housing/basic-needs support with access confirmation
McKinney-Vento support when a family may be homeless or doubled up: contact Bryant Martin (martinb@grps.org) or Mosuray McSwain (McSwainM@grps.org)
Family intervention plan that accounts for current instability
Physical health: School health plan / nurse or health aide coordination
Return-to-school intervention plan around health needs
Warm connection to health care/community support when access is the barrier
Mental health / school refusal: Coordinated re-entry/intervention plan with appropriate Behavioral Health/Counseling support
Gradual return or transition support when determined appropriate by the school team
Warm connection to community mental-health support when access is needed
Belonging / relationships: School response to bullying, climate or relationship concern
Morning / family routines: Short-cycle FSS follow-up on the routine and attendance
Engagement / motivation: Expanded learning, mentoring or enrichment connection
School engagement / relevance strategy tied to scholar goals
Safety / bullying / discipline: School-controlled discipline/process correction tied to return and belonging

bd.title: Transportation
bd.desc: Getting to school consistently is difficult or unreliable.
ask: What part of the trip breaks down?
Is the issue daily, occasional or tied to a schedule?
What has the family already tried?
bd.f: Understand the family situation; build the intervention plan; monitor whether attendance improves.
bd.k: Coordinate community/partner options when a resource connection is needed.
bd.s: Check school-controlled transportation processes, schedule and arrival supports.
bd.sh: Confirm one plan and whether the transportation barrier actually changed.

bd.title: Housing / basic needs
bd.desc: Housing instability, utilities, food, clothing or other basic needs affect attendance.
ask: What immediate need is affecting attendance?
Is housing stable right now?
What support is already connected?
bd.f: Caring inquiry, scholar/family intervention and sustained follow-up.
bd.k: Coordinate community resources, partners and access.
bd.s: Activate appropriate district/school supports and remove school barriers.
bd.sh: Warm handoff, confirm access and keep the identified goal visible.

bd.title: Physical health
bd.desc: Illness, chronic health needs, appointments or access to care affect attendance.
ask: What health issue is affecting attendance?
Is there a care plan or provider?
What makes returning to school difficult?
bd.f: Understand family impact; support intervention planning and follow-up.
bd.s: Nurse/health aide and school team address school-based health access/accommodations.
bd.sh: Coordinate without duplicating clinical or school health functions.

bd.title: Mental health / school refusal
bd.desc: Anxiety, distress, avoidance or other mental health concerns may be connected to absence.
ask: What happens before the scholar misses school?
What does the scholar say about coming to school?
Are there safety concerns requiring immediate professional response?
look: Behavioral health/counseling information available to the team
bd.f: Caring conversation, family engagement and scholar/family intervention.
bd.s: Behavioral Health/Counseling and school team address school-controlled conditions and appropriate supports.
bd.sh: One coordinated plan with appropriate professional roles clearly protected.

bd.title: Academic access / challenge
bd.desc: Academic difficulty, missed learning, course access or instructional conditions contribute to absence.
ask: Which classes/times are hardest to attend?
Is the scholar avoiding work they feel unable to complete?
What would make re-entry manageable?
bd.f: Bring scholar/family perspective into the intervention plan and monitor attendance.
bd.k: Connect expanded learning/community opportunities when they add value.
bd.s: Own academic/instructional response, re-entry, tutoring/intervention and access.
bd.sh: Align academic support with the identified goal.

bd.title: Belonging / relationships
bd.desc: The scholar does not feel connected, welcomed, known or safe at school.
ask: Who at school does the scholar trust?
Where/when does the scholar feel disconnected?
What would make school feel more welcoming?
bd.f: Build trust, elevate scholar/family voice and monitor progress and impact.
bd.k: Support engagement, enrichment, mentoring or community connections where appropriate.
bd.s: Own school climate, relationships, safety and belonging conditions.
bd.sh: Coordinate a relationship-centered response and review whether belonging improves.

bd.title: Morning / family routines
bd.desc: Sleep, caregiving, work schedules or morning routines interfere with getting to school.
ask: Walk me through a typical school morning.
Where does the routine break down?
What small change would make tomorrow easier?
bd.f: Lead family-centered problem-solving, routines and sustained follow-up.
bd.k: Connect resources only when a community support is part of the barrier solution.
bd.s: Consider arrival/re-entry supports and school-controlled schedule issues.
bd.sh: Avoid multiple staff giving the family competing plans.

bd.title: Engagement / motivation
bd.desc: The scholar sees limited value in attending or is disconnected from learning/opportunities.
ask: What makes school worth coming to?
What interests or goals matter to the scholar?
When is attendance strongest?
bd.f: Use caring conversation and intervention planning tied to scholar goals.
bd.k: Connect programs, enrichment, mentoring and community opportunities.
bd.s: Strengthen relevance, relationships, instructional engagement and school opportunities.
bd.sh: Build one engagement strategy around the scholar's strengths.

bd.title: Safety / bullying / discipline
bd.desc: A school-controlled safety, bullying, discipline or re-entry issue may be driving absence.
ask: Where/when does the scholar feel unsafe or unwelcome?
Is there a specific incident, person or setting?
What needs to change at school?
bd.f: Support family voice and attendance follow-through; do not own the school-controlled fix.
bd.k: Coordinate partners if an external/community support is needed.
bd.s: Own safety, bullying, discipline, restorative/re-entry and school-process response.
bd.sh: Keep attendance support coordinated while the school removes the school-controlled barrier.
